title: Canonical comparison of normalized and embedding finite-field scalar extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, a Noetherian finite-dimensional scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible, and finite coefficient fields $E\subset F$ in $\Omega$. Use the canonical small coefficient models and completed coefficient maps of [def-weil-pbc-finite-completed-coefficient-map]. Let $Q_E$ denote the integral localization, and $S_{E,F}$ the normalized finite-stage transition of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category]. Let $S^{\rm raw}_{E,F}$ be the embedding scalar extension of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension], evaluated on these same small fields and their transported inclusion. Define $c_{E,F}:S_{E,F}\xrightarrow\sim S^{\rm raw}_{E,F}$ as the unique natural isomorphism whose component on every integral object $Q_E(K)$ is the specified integral/rational scalar comparison of [def-weil-pbc-finite-stage-pair-category], under the canonical equality of the actual completed coefficient maps and hence the integral tensor objects. The equality is fixed by all finite quotient projections, which are the same transported field inclusion. At $E=F$ this comparison is precisely the specified tensor-multiplication unit. This defines a comparison of the two existing scalar constructions, without choosing a new coefficient map or discarding the reflexive case.
